definition: The specific sound recording of a song, usually owned by a label or the artist. Sampling it needs its owner's permission.
The song itself, words, music and melody, owned by its writers and publishers, separate from any recording of it.
Getting written permission from every owner of a sampled recording and song, ideally before release.
A specialist who identifies the owners of a sample, negotiates with them and papers the deal.
Money paid up front for permission to use a sample, separate from any ongoing royalty.
The percentage of ownership in the new song that goes to the writers and publishers of the sampled song.
A percentage of the new recording's revenue paid to the owner of the sampled recording.
Dividing a fee or percentage among owners in proportion to each one's stake.
A deal term under which every owner gets terms as good as the best any other owner gets.
Part of an existing song re-recorded from scratch without the original audio. The US Copyright Office says it needs the song owner's permission and not the recording owner's.
A new recording made to match a sampled passage closely, so the original master is not used. The publishing still has to be cleared.
A recording made to resemble another one. It involves no master license, but the underlying song still needs permission.
A new recording of an existing song that leaves its basic melody and character unchanged.
The US mechanism that lets a musician record a cover of a released song at a set rate. It grants nothing in anyone's recording.
A US defense weighed case by case; the Copyright Office says there is no formula and only a court can decide it.
A license with no further payments after the first. The sound is licensed for use in new tracks; the buyer does not own it.
A license that leaves the seller free to license the same sound or beat to other people.
A limited license to a producer's beat, which can carry stream caps and an expiry date.
YouTube's audio fingerprinting system. DistroKid says tracks built on shared royalty-free loops are ineligible for its Content ID add-on.
A writing session organized by a publisher; some now start from old hits in the publisher's own catalog.
A company that holds rights to existing songs or recordings, such as a label, publisher or investment-backed fund, and collects when they are sampled.
